sentences.text: Rawatbhata Dist Chittorgarh

. (Presently Lodged In Dist Jail Chittorgarh)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp
----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Rajesh Kumar
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Urja Ram Kalbi, Public Prosecutor  Mr. Ojas Shakdwipeeya for  complainant  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 11/03/2025 1.

This application for bail under Section 483 BNSS (old Section 439 Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.138/2024 registered at Police Station Rawatbhata, District Chittorgarh for the offences under Sections 363, 342, 376-D & 120B IPC and Sections 3/4, 5(g)/6 & 16/17 of the POCSO Act.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that co-accused persons namely Vishakha Patil S/o Rakesh Patil, Dhirendra Singh Deora @ Boby S/o Narendra Singh Deora (S.B. Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.12845/2024) and Suresh Gurjar S/o Girdhari Gurjar, Sudhanshu Mishra S/o Shailendra Mishra (S.B. Criminal [2025:RJ-JD:13583] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-14775/2024] Misc. Bail Application No.10782/2024) have already been enlarged on bail by the Co-ordinate Benches of this Court vide orders dated 06.11.2024 and 17.09.2024.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has falsely been implicated in the present case.

Drawing attention of this Court to the FIR and various other documents attached with the case file, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that sufficient material is available on record to indicate that on the date of the alleged incident, victim voluntarily eloped with the present petitioner and thereafter remained in his company for about 12 hours.
Later on, when the relations between the parties turned sour, the petitioner has been roped in a false criminal case.

Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner is 18 years old and in judicial custody since 21.06.2024; the investigation against the petitioner has already been completed and trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused-petitioner.
5. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the bail application.

However,
learned counsel Mr. Ojas Shakdwipeeya appearing for the complainant submitted that during pendency of the present bail application, the parties have entered into a compromise and decided to settle the disputes amicably in the spirit of Lok Adalat and therefore, he has no objection in case the petitioner is enlarged on bail.

Learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant were also not in a position to refute the fact that the above named co-accused [2025:RJ-JD:13583]
(3 of 3) [CRLMB-14775/2024] persons have already been enlarged on bail by the co-ordinate Benches of this Court.

6. Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case and without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
7. Consequently, the bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Harsh Rethudiya @ Aasu S/o Santosh Rethudiya, arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.138/2024 registered at Police Station Rawatbhata, District Chittorgarh shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial Court, for his appearance before that Court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
8. It is however, made clear that findings recorded/observations made above are for limited purposes of adjudication of bail application.
The trial Court shall not get prejudiced by the same.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 10-T.Singh/-
